meta.name: Send SAP XML sales orders from GoHighLevel to a warehouse via Make.com SFTP

name: Send Order to Warehouse through SFTP

parameters.content:
## 📦 Send Order to Warehouse via SFTP

### How it works
When a sales opportunity is created or updated in GoHighLevel (GHL), a webhook fires and triggers this workflow. The opportunity ID is used to pull the full opportunity details from the LeadConnector API, then fetch all associated product records. Products are split out individually, filtered to exclude non-product relations, and enriched with their full product details — including SAP codes and quantities. A code node assembles a standards-compliant SAP XML sales order with a generated order number, today's date, and one sales line per product. The XML is converted to a binary file and posted to a Make.com webhook, which handles the final SFTP upload to the warehouse ERP system.

### Setup steps
1. Set the **Webhook** node to receive POST requests from your GHL workflow trigger.
2. Add your **LeadConnector API key** to the Authorization header in the three GHL HTTP Request nodes.
3. In the `Build SAP XML Sales Order` code node, update the `YOUR_SAP_CUSTOMER_NUMBER`, `YOUR_SAP_COMPANY_CODE`, and `YOUR_SAP_PARTNER_ID` placeholders to match your SAP configuration, or replace with dynamic GHL account lookups.
4. Create a Make.com scenario that receives a file via webhook and uploads it to your warehouse SFTP server. Replace `YOUR_MAKE_SCENARIO_WEBHOOK_ID` in the final HTTP node.
5. Test end-to-end with a real opportunity ID using the webhook test URL.

## 🔗 GHL Webhook Intake
Receives the POST from your GoHighLevel automation when an opportunity is created or updated. The payload must include `opportunity_id` in the body — this ID drives every subsequent API call in the workflow.

## 🔍 Opportunity & Product Data Fetch
Three sequential LeadConnector API calls: fetch the opportunity, fetch its related associations, then fetch the full product record for each association. Products without an SAP code or quantity are filtered out before building the order.

## 🧾 SAP XML Order Assembly
Builds a standards-compliant SAP XML sales order document — order number from the opportunity ID, today's date, customer number, company code, and one `<SalesLine>` block per product with its SAP product code and quantity. The filename follows the pattern `Distinct_Sales_YYYYMMDD.xml`.

## 📤 File Conversion & SFTP Delivery
Converts the XML string to a binary file, then POSTs it to a Make.com webhook which handles the final SFTP upload to the warehouse ERP. Using Make.com here avoids needing direct SFTP credentials inside n8n.

## 🔑 Credentials & Endpoints
- **LeadConnector (GHL) API key** — add to Authorization header in all three GHL HTTP nodes
- **Make.com webhook URL** — replace `YOUR_MAKE_SCENARIO_WEBHOOK_ID` in the final HTTP node
- SAP `customerNumber` and `Company` are currently hardcoded in the code node — update before going live.
